feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence from earlier races: iteration 1 (mass 0.6, track 0.10, score 114.39) is the reference, with oval progress 0.47, oval oscillation 0.28 and max_error 0.061 to 0.066 m. Iteration 7 (track 0.11) cut oscillation to 0.259 but cut oval progress to 0.416, so extra damping costs progress. Iteration 8 (track 0.09) kept progress near iteration 1 (oval 0.456) with oscillation 0.251, so the track is near its optimum. Iteration 4 (mass 0.5 with a faster drivetrain) raised oscillation to 0.33, so less inertia makes the robot twitchier. Sensor lead 0.02 m and 0.04 m both scored below 0.03 m, and the 5-sensor 12 mm layout is the best measured. Integration point: I kept the iteration-1 controller exactly, so the only change in the race is mass. Heavier mass adds yaw inertia and traction, which should slow the overshoot. Change the next design by what the race shows. If oscillation falls to about 0.28 or below and oval progress holds at or above 0.47, mass is a real lever: try 0.9 kg next. If oscillation falls but progress drops below about 0.44, the extra inertia is slowing the turn, so return to 0.6 kg and use controller damping instead. If oscillation is unchanged, mass is not the limit, and the remaining gain must come from the controller.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation falls to about 0.28 or below on the oval and oval progress holds at or above 0.47, set mass to 0.9 kg (from 0.8). Iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.064 to 0.066 m with small rms_error, so the excursion is bend overshoot that more yaw inertia should damp.

If oval progress falls below about 0.44 with lower oscillation, return mass to 0.6 kg (iteration 1) and keep wheel_track 0.10 m. Iteration 7 showed that damping bought by a geometry change can cost progress, so the balance point is near iteration 1.
Keep the five-sensor 12 mm layout at y 0.03 m (x -0.05 to +0.05). Iteration 5 (lead 0.02 m, score 91.8) and iteration 6 (lead 0.04 m, score 109.9) both fell below iteration 1.
